transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been having these really late work nights lately. I'm a graphic designer, and I have this one client right now who is just impossible. They keep changing their mind on this logo's color palette. We completely agreed on this really nice muted sage green, and yesterday they emailed me asking for neon? Which makes literally no sense for an organic bakery. It's just so frustrating. 

But anyway, because I'm up so late dealing with all those last-minute revisions, I’ll order what I tell myself is just a normal dinner. Except... it turns into a whole entrée, and then sides, and a dessert, and then I end up grabbing extra snacks from my kitchen on top of all of it. It's way, way more than I’d ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me. But yeah, I spent like three hours last night just trying to make neon green look organic...
Do you think you eat more when you're stressed or frustrated, like with this client?

I mean, maybe? I haven't really noticed if it's the stress specifically. I'm just sitting there staring at my screen. But honestly, it's hard not to be stressed when people don't understand basic design principles. Like, I had this other client last year who wanted me to design a logo for a meditation app, and they insisted on using fire engine red. Red! For a calming meditation space! I tried to explain how color psychology works, but they just wouldn't listen to me. I actually ended up having to drop them because it was going to completely ruin my portfolio. Oh, and my dog, Barnaby, he always gets so needy when I'm working late on stuff like that, too. He'll just sit under my desk and whine and paw at my leg while I'm trying to focus on my monitor, which doesn't help anything. 

Um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right. Yeah, I don't know, I haven't really paid attention to whether it's the frustration causing the eating.
Do you usually eat more when you're feeling upset or anxious?

Um, upset or anxious? I don't know, maybe? I haven't really tracked it like that. I just know I eat a lot when I'm working late. Like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I've eaten everything. But honestly, it's hard not to be anxious lately. My sister is planning her wedding, and she wants me to do all the invitations, the menus, the seating charts... everything. And she's being a total bridezilla about it. She wants this specific shade of blush pink that is just impossible to print consistently. I swear, I've gone through three different local printers, and none of them can get it right. The last guy I talked to at the print shop was so rude about it, too. He acted like I was being unreasonable, but I'm just trying to make my sister happy, you know? And Barnaby—my dog—he chewed up one of the test prints yesterday, which just added to the chaos. 

Wait, sorry, what was the question again? About being upset? Yeah, I'm not really sure if that's what triggers the eating. I just haven't noticed.
Do you think your eating changes when you're feeling anxious or upset?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? I really don't know, I'm sorry. Like I said, I haven't really noticed if being upset or anxious changes anything. I just know the eating happens when I'm up late working. 

And speaking of being up late, my sister actually called me at 11:30 last night completely freaking out about the bridesmaid dresses. She picked this chiffon fabric that literally wrinkles if you even look at it wrong. My cousin Sarah is refusing to wear it because she says it washes her out, which, honestly, she's not wrong. Sarah has this very warm skin undertone, and the dress is this icy pastel color. It's a disaster waiting to happen. I told my sister she should just let us pick our own styles in the same color family, but she is obsessed with everyone matching perfectly for the photos. She hired this ridiculously expensive photographer, too, like thousands of dollars just for a few hours, so I guess I get why she's being so particular, but still. It's exhausting dealing with it all. 

But anyway, yeah, no, I haven't tracked if anxiety makes me eat differently. I just honestly don't know.
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're stressed or frustrated with work or other things?

Does it make me feel better? Um... I don't know. Maybe? I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess in the moment I'm not really thinking about feeling better or not. 

But honestly, you know what would actually make me feel better? If my sister just eloped. Seriously, the venue she picked is this converted barn out in the country. Which sounds cute, right? Rustic chic or whatever. But it's in the middle of literally nowhere, and the cell service is completely nonexistent. I was out there with her last weekend to look at the lighting setup because she wants this very specific fairy-light canopy, and my phone was just a brick the entire time. Which is an absolute nightmare when you're a freelancer waiting on client feedback. I had this one client who needed a rush revision on a digital brochure by 5 PM, and I couldn't even get the PDF to attach to my email. I had to drive three miles down a literal dirt road just to get one bar of signal so it would send. My car was completely covered in dust by the time I got back, and Barnaby was in the backseat just sneezing non-stop from it... 

Anyway, sorry, what did you ask? If the eating makes me feel better? Yeah, I really don't know. I've just never paid attention to whether it actually helps with the stress.
Do you think eating is something you do to cope with stress?

Wait, coping with stress? I mean... I feel like you've kind of asked me this a few times now in different ways. And honestly, my answer is still just... I don't know. I really couldn't tell you if I'm doing it to cope. I'm just eating. 

But speaking of coping, I really don't know how my mom is coping with all this wedding stuff either. She offered to pay for the floral arrangements, which was super nice of her, but my sister took that as a blank check to hire this boutique florist who only works with locally sourced, organic, pesticide-free blooms. Which, fine, whatever, save the bees, but the quote they gave my mom was astronomical. Like, you could buy a decent used car for what these flowers cost. And half of them are basically weeds! My mom called me yesterday practically in tears because she doesn't want to tell my sister she can't afford it, but she also can't pull that kind of money out of thin air. I told her to just be honest, but my mom hates conflict. She'll probably just put it on a credit card and stress about it for the next five years. It's so ridiculous. 

But yeah, the eating and coping thing... I just don't know. I've never really analyzed it like that.
Do you usually eat this much when you're alone, or is it just when you're working late?

Well, yeah, it's definitely only when I'm alone. Like, if I'm out with friends or having lunch with coworkers, I'm super careful to just eat a normal amount, or even less. I'll get a salad or something. But when I'm alone in my condo, especially after midnight, that's when it happens. I even close the blinds and make sure to throw away all the delivery containers right away because I would be absolutely mortified if anyone saw how much food there was. 

Which, honestly, getting rid of trash in my building is its own complete nightmare right now. The condo association decided to switch waste management companies last month to save a few bucks, and it has been a disaster. The new company only picks up the recycling every other week, and they completely got rid of the large item dumpster. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she's like eighty, she tried to throw away this old broken microwave, and the super actually knocked on her door and made her drag it back into her apartment! Can you imagine? And the regular trash chutes are always jammed now because people are trying to stuff oversized garbage bags down them instead of taking them to the basement. I had to carry a bag down three flights of stairs yesterday because the elevator was being serviced—again. They just raised our HOA fees by fifteen percent, and for what? Broken elevators and overflowing trash chutes. It's infuriating. 

But yeah, to answer your question, I definitely only eat like that when I'm completely alone. I could never do it in front of anyone else.
Do you think you would eat this much if you weren't feeling stressed or frustrated?

I mean, if I wasn't stressed? I really couldn't say. I just... I don't know if the stress has anything to do with it, honestly. I've never really tried to connect the two. 

But speaking of stress, you know what's really stressing me out right now? My car's registration is due, and the DMV website is completely broken. Like, I spent an hour yesterday just trying to log in. Every time I hit submit, it just gave me this weird error code. I even tried calling them, which, you know, is basically a joke. I was on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this awful elevator music that sounded like it was recorded underwater. And then, when a real person finally answered, we got disconnected after like two seconds! I swear, it's like they design the system specifically to make you lose your mind. Now I have to actually go down there in person, which means taking time off work, and the line is always wrapped around the building by 8 AM. It's just ridiculous. 

But yeah, about the eating... I really have no idea if I'd still do it if I wasn't frustrated with things. I just don't know.
Do you usually try to hide the fact that you're eating this much from others?

Wait, hide the fact that I'm eating? I mean, I thought I just answered that, didn't I? I told you about how I only do it when I'm alone and how I throw away all the delivery containers right away. I'm pretty sure I already went over all that. 

But speaking of hiding things, you wouldn't believe what my cousin Mark is trying to hide from his wife right now. He bought this ridiculously expensive vintage electric guitar—like, we're talking thousands of dollars—and he's keeping it at my aunt's house because he doesn't want his wife to find out. He told her he was saving up for a down payment on a new house, but instead, he blew a huge chunk of it on this guitar that he can't even play that well! He's only been taking lessons for like six months. And the worst part is, my aunt is totally enabling him. She thinks it's hilarious, but I told her, when his wife finds out—and she will find out—it is going to be World War III. They already fight all the time about money. I honestly don't know how they're still married. It's just so deceitful, you know? 

But yeah, about hiding the food... I really feel like we already talked about that. I definitely hide it.
Do you feel like eating helps you deal with your stress and frustration?

Does it help? Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether it actually makes me feel better or if it's just something I do. I don't know if "helps" is the right word. 

But speaking of frustration, oh my god, you would not believe the client I'm dealing with right now at work. I'm a graphic designer, right? And this woman hired me to redesign her bakery's logo. She explicitly told me she wanted something "minimalist and modern." So I spent three days drafting these really clean, beautiful concepts with this gorgeous sans-serif typography. I send them over, and she emails me back saying, "Where are the cartoon cupcakes? I want a giant pink cupcake with googly eyes." Googly eyes! On a modern logo! I tried to explain to her that it totally clashes with the brand identity we discussed, but she just wouldn't listen. And then she had the nerve to ask if I could do it for half the price since "adding a cupcake is easy." I swear, people think graphic design is just clicking a magic button on Photoshop. It's so insulting to my profession. I've been doing this since I got my degree and it never ends with these people. 

So yeah... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, if eating helps the stress. I mean, I guess I don't really know. I just haven't noticed if it actually fixes anything.
Do you think you eat as a way to deal with your feelings?

Deal with my feelings? I mean... I don't really know. I've never really stopped to analyze if it's an emotional thing or what. I just haven't really thought about it like that. 

But speaking of feelings, my sister is having a lot of feelings lately about her wedding. She's getting married in October, and she decided to make all the bridesmaids' dresses herself. Which, okay, ambitious, right? Especially since she barely knows how to sew! She bought this vintage sewing machine from a thrift store, and it keeps jamming. Yesterday, she called me literally sobbing because she accidentally sewed the sleeve of the maid of honor's dress to the hem. I told her to just buy them off the rack—there are so many good options online now—but she's so stubborn. She wants that "handmade rustic aesthetic" for the photos. It's driving the whole bridal party crazy. My mom is actually threatening to secretly hire a tailor to fix everything behind her back so we don't all walk down the aisle looking like we're wearing potato sacks. It's just a total mess. 

But anyway... what did you ask? Oh, right, if I eat because of my feelings. Yeah, I just really couldn't say. I haven't noticed if that's why I do it.
Do you think you would still eat this much if you weren't working late and dealing with stressful situations?

If I wasn't working late? I mean, I guess I'm not really sure. I haven't really had a period where I wasn't stressed out to compare it to, so I don't know what I would do. 

But speaking of working late, my friend Sarah just got a job at this new tech startup, and they do a four-day work week. Can you imagine? She has every single Friday off. And not only that, but they have this strict rule where they actually lock everyone out of the company Slack and email servers at 5 PM on Thursday. Like, you physically cannot log in to work even if you wanted to. She was telling me about it this weekend when we went to this farmer's market—which, by the way, was totally overpriced. They were charging like eight dollars for a single heirloom tomato. Who pays eight dollars for a tomato? 

Anyway, Sarah says her productivity has actually gone up since she started there because she's so well-rested. I pitched the idea of just leaving at 5 PM to my boss, and he basically laughed in my face. He's one of those "hustle culture" guys who thinks if you aren't grinding 60 hours a week, you're lazy. It's so toxic. 

But yeah, wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, if I'd still eat like that without the stress. I honestly couldn't tell you. It's just hard to say since I'm pretty much always stressed.
Do you think you eat when you're alone as a way to comfort yourself?

Comfort myself? Um... I don't know, honestly. I haven't really paid attention to whether it's about comfort or just... I don't know, just something that happens when I'm by myself. 

But speaking of being alone, I actually just started trying to grow my own houseplants because my apartment felt so empty. I bought this fiddle leaf fig, which everyone on Instagram makes look so easy, right? They just stick it in a corner and it looks like a magazine shoot. Well, let me tell you, those things are so incredibly dramatic. If you move it two inches to the left, it drops three leaves. If you look at it wrong, it turns brown. I bought this special moisture meter and this expensive organic fertilizer, and I swear it's still dying. I was at the garden center for like two hours on Sunday just talking to this guy who works there—I think his name was Gary—about soil drainage. He was telling me about how people overwater them because they think they're being nice, but they're actually drowning the roots. It's crazy how much science goes into just keeping a plant alive in your living room. 

So... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, about eating for comfort when I'm alone. Yeah, I'm really not sure about that. I just haven't thought about it in those terms.
Do you think you eat more when you're feeling emotionally overwhelmed?

Emotionally overwhelmed? I mean... I guess I've never really tracked it like that to see if there's a connection. I just don't know. 

But speaking of being overwhelmed, I have this freelance client right now who is driving me absolutely up the wall. I'm doing a brand redesign for her artisanal dog bakery, right? And she tells me she wants the logo to really pop and be super vibrant, but her mandatory color palette is literally just beige, slate gray, and taupe. I spent three hours on Zoom with her on Tuesday trying to explain basic color theory, and she just kept sending me links to these minimalist Pinterest boards that were basically just empty circles. And then, get this, she asked if we could use Papyrus for the main font. Papyrus! I'm a professional graphic designer, I can't put Papyrus in my portfolio. I actually asked her if she'd seen that old comedy sketch with Ryan Gosling about it, but she had no idea what I was talking about. I'm dreading our next check-in call so much. 

But anyway, sorry, I totally lost my train of thought. You were asking about being overwhelmed and eating? Yeah, I honestly couldn't say. I just haven't really noticed if that makes me do it more or not.
Do you think you eat as a way to make yourself feel better when you're upset?

Make myself feel better? Um... I don't really know. I've never really thought about it like that, like if I'm doing it specifically because I'm upset. 

But you know what did upset me recently? I took my car in for just a regular oil change, right? And the mechanic comes out with this clipboard looking all serious, telling me I need new brake pads, new rotors, a new cabin air filter, and that my transmission fluid is practically sludge. He quoted me like twelve hundred dollars! I was so mad because I just had it inspected six months ago and everything was fine. I actually called my dad from the waiting room because he used to rebuild old muscle cars in the nineties, and he told me to ask the guy to physically show me the brake pads. When I asked him to do that, suddenly he was like, "Well, they're in the yellow zone, you could probably wait until your next service." It's just so frustrating how they try to upsell you the second you walk in the door. I ended up just getting the oil change and leaving, but I was fuming the whole drive home. 

Wait, what were we just talking about? Oh, eating when I'm upset. Yeah, I don't really know if I do that. I just haven't really made that connection.
Do you think eating helps you cope with feeling stressed?

Stressed? I mean, I guess I've never really sat down and thought about whether eating is a coping mechanism for stress. I don't really know if they're linked like that for me. 

But talking about stress, you wouldn't believe the week I've had with my upstairs neighbors. They just got this puppy—a husky mix, I think—and they leave it alone all day while they're at work. It literally howls for eight hours straight. I tried to be cool about it, you know? I left a really polite note on their door with a little drawing of a dog, just saying, "Hey, not sure if you know, but your pup is pretty vocal when you're gone." And the guy actually came down and knocked on my door at like 9 PM, totally defensive, saying his dog is crate-trained and I must be hearing things. Hearing things! The walls in this building are paper thin. I can hear when he drops his keys, let alone a dog singing the song of its people all afternoon. I had to buy these expensive noise-canceling headphones just to get any work done, but they give me a headache if I wear them for more than an hour. 

Anyway... sorry, I get so worked up about it. What did you ask? Oh, right, eating to cope with stress. Honestly, I'm just not sure. I haven't really paid attention to whether stress is what triggers it.
Do you think you eat as a way to deal with difficult emotions?

Difficult emotions? Um... I don't know. I guess I just haven't really stepped back to analyze if I'm eating because I'm feeling something difficult, you know? It's hard to say.

But speaking of difficult, my sister is getting married next month, and the bridesmaid dress situation has been a total nightmare. She picked out this specific shade of sage green, but she wants us all to pick our own styles, which sounds great in theory, right? But she keeps vetoing everything I send her. I found this gorgeous A-line chiffon dress that would be perfect for a June wedding, and she told me the neckline was "too aggressive." Too aggressive! It was a basic sweetheart neckline. Then she suggested this halter top thing that literally only looks good if you have the exact body type of a 1990s supermodel. I swear, she's turning into a complete bridezilla, and my mom is just enabling her. My mom actually called me yesterday to suggest I wear Spanx under whatever dress I end up with, which, thanks Mom, really appreciate the confidence boost. I spent half the morning looking at dresses online and just wanting to scream.

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. What was the question? Dealing with difficult emotions and eating? Yeah, I really couldn't tell you. I just haven't noticed if there's a link there.
Do you think you eat when you're feeling sad or upset?

Sad or upset? I mean... maybe? I really haven't kept track of it like that. I don't know if I can say for sure that feeling sad is what makes me eat. 

Though honestly, I was pretty upset yesterday. I had this huge deadline for a branding package for a new client—this boutique coffee shop downtown. I spent three weeks perfecting their logo, getting the typography exactly how they described they wanted it in the brief. I sent over the final proofs, and the owner emails me back saying, "Actually, we decided to go in a more minimalist direction, can you just use Helvetica and make it black and white?" Helvetica! After I custom-drew this beautiful retro-inspired font for them! I was so frustrated I almost cried. It's like people think graphic design is just pushing a button on a computer. And the worst part is, they still expect it by Friday, which means I have to scrap weeks of work and start over, but they don't want to pay for the extra revisions because they claim it's "simpler" now. 

Oh, gosh, sorry. I'm venting again. You asked about eating when I'm sad, right? Yeah, I just... I'm not sure. I haven't really noticed a specific pattern with that.
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're feeling overwhelmed?

Overwhelmed? I... I don't know. I guess I've never really stopped to think if being overwhelmed is what sets it off. It's hard to say if it actually makes me feel better. 

But speaking of overwhelmed, my car started making this horrible grinding noise yesterday on the way to the grocery store. It's a 2012 Honda, so it's getting up there in mileage, but I just put new brakes on it last month. I took it to this mechanic near my apartment, and he kept talking down to me, like explaining what a transmission is in this super slow, condescending voice. I know what a transmission is! I just don't know why it sounds like there are rocks in my engine. Then he hands me an estimate for twelve hundred dollars and tells me I shouldn't drive it until it's fixed. Twelve hundred dollars! I don't just have that sitting around, especially not with the wedding coming up and having to buy a new dress because of my sister. Now I have to figure out the bus schedule, which is a nightmare in my neighborhood, or pay for rideshares everywhere. I spent an hour last night just staring at the estimate, trying to figure out how I'm going to budget for it. 

Wait, sorry. I'm completely off track again. What was it you asked? Eating when I'm overwhelmed? Yeah, honestly, I just couldn't tell you. I haven't really connected the dots on that one.
Do you think eating is something you do to make yourself feel better when you're upset or stressed?

Stressed? Um, I guess I just don't really know. I've never really sat down and tracked if I'm eating specifically because of stress, you know? It's just hard to pinpoint a reason like that. 

But oh my gosh, speaking of stress, my upstairs neighbor has been driving me absolutely insane lately. I'm pretty sure he bought a treadmill, or maybe a rowing machine? I don't know what it is, but every morning at exactly 5:15 AM, it sounds like a herd of elephants is stampeding right above my bedroom ceiling. And my apartment has those exposed pipes—which looked super cool and industrial when I signed the lease—but they rattle so loudly now. I actually went up there on Tuesday and left a really polite note on his door, just asking if he could maybe work out at, like, 7 AM instead. And you know what he did? He slid the note back under *my* door with a sticky note on it that just said "Earplugs are cheap." Can you believe that? The nerve of some people! I pay way too much in rent to be woken up before the sun rises by someone else's cardio routine. I even tried emailing the property manager, but she's completely useless and just said it's "normal apartment living noise." 

Oh, wow, I'm so sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. You were asking if I eat to make myself feel better when I'm stressed? Yeah, I really don't have a good answer for you. I just haven't noticed if they're actually connected.
